newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Long term prices key to U.K. rates - Burns.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Long term prices key to U.K. rates - Burns.

text.p: British Treasury permanent secretary Sir Terence Burns said on Wednesday monetary policy had to be set with an eye on inflation two years away and suggested there should be less emphasis on recent inflation information.
"Time lags are mainly a problem for monetary policy," Burns told an economists conference here.

"Interest rates have to be set today in order to influence inflation on average two years on. This challenges our ability to see the future and suggests that we should give less emphasis to the most recent inflation data," he siad.
Such lags were also a problem for fiscal policy, he said.
"One crucial uncertainty which is itself compounded by the existence of time lags is the position of output in relation to its underlying trend," he said.

"This is important both for monetary policy, where pressure on resources is a crucial input to interest rate decisions, and for fiscal policy, where the cycle plays such a big part in the outcome for tax collection and expenditure and confuses the picture of underlying public finances." Britain last cut its key base rate by 25 basis points to 5.75 percent on June 6.
